title: Clang! Clang!
subtitle: The relentless toil, all for the sake of their eyes.

trails.title: Research Log
trails.description: In the name of London, the current Fogwalker has put forth great effort. Records show sacrifices of sleep, numerous attempts at amateur Arcane Skill enchantment, and a few rather ungentlemanly words.

content.text: London Air Pollution Auto-Detect Cleaner Research Notes

Improved Suction Device - Third Test

Unsuccessful again. Not surprising—a mere cleaning device cannot possibly hope to replace the role of the Fogwalker lineage. Amplifying the family's Arcane Skill may hold some promise, but ... we've only three weeks left.

Truth is, my goal is not to solve the unsolvable mysteries of the industrial era—I simply need to ensure that breathable air is available to all for the event's duration. That means faster filtering, broader reach, larger capacity—just for a short period of time, not forever.

Arcane Skill Boosting Device - Fourth Test

I could be off the mark on this one. Boosting the potency of arcane skills showed very limited effects. This line of thought failed to meet expectations, miserably so. It was a bloody waste of time!

Air Pollution Purifier - First Test

Thanks to the St. Pavlov Foundation for their ritual inscription techniques, the device works!

I was on the right track, somewhat. The Fogwalker's Arcane Skill may be irreplaceable, but this essentially doubles the number of hands we've got. By inscribing incantations onto a device like this, it's like having a duplicate of myself, working in tandem with me. Sadly, I'm not capable of supporting more than one of these, and the purification efficiency is still subpar ...

Air Pollution Purifier MK. III - First Test

A complete catastrophe! I'm a fool, an idiot, a nincompoop! Curse it, curse it!

Advanced Air Pollution Purifier - Third Test

What an astounding discovery by the Foundation! I've never heard of enchanting arcane skills onto everyday, ordinary items before; their developments in this area are revolutionary. Though I lack the expertise to perform true enchantment, following their instructions to combine specific tools has improved my Arcane Skill's integration into the device! And by integrating components of human technology ... I've achieved success! I shall name this creation the "London Air Pollution Auto-Detecting Purifier."

London Air Pollution Auto-Detect Cleaner MK. III - Seventh Test

Phenomenal! Maintaining the purification output puts an extraordinary strain on me, but at least it is sustainable for several hours. I pray that tomorrow's demonstration goes off without a hitch.

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: Outta the way, outta the way! I've found the perfect component for Mr. Fog's machine!
The boy darts through the bustling alley, slipping between the hats in the smog, and landing among the crowd at the corner of the square.
The machine, about half the size of a person, is at the center of everyone's attention. The crowd members whisper to each other in excited tones.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: This allows us to analyze the composition of the atmosphere.
He lifts his head above the crowd, his voice cutting through the chatter.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: If the color of the filter paper meets that of the pollution standard, it will determine that the air is polluted and start working automatically.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Let me show you.
Heads turn as the crowd stares intently at the measuring tool in Mr. Fog's hands.

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: Scuse me! Oi, Mr. Fog, look, I found a glass stopper! It's the one you were lookin' for, right?
Stopper in hand, Freddy eagerly pushes through the crowd toward Mr. Fog.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Oh, you found it! Yes, that's exactly what I need!
He gratefully takes the stopper.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Your attention, please! This glass stopper is one of the core components of this machine, which can harness the power of the sun to purify the air. Of course, this is only one component of many.

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Are you done talkin'? We've given you everythin' you need. Where's our purification machine?

items.speaker: Neighbor I
items.text: Quite right! We need to see the purification machine!
Discontent and suspicion start to surface among the crowd.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: No need to worry, folks. Believe me. There is no one who wants this purification machine to work more than I. So, I've been doing some experiments.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Arthur, mate!

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Here!
Mr. Fog looks across the crowd, his eyes bright with intent, prompting the crowd to part a path along the line of his gaze.
Brimley, Tooth Fairy, and three dockworkers appear at the end of the path. They're hauling a cart carrying a heavy machine.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Forgive me for not helping move it. I'm afraid I'm handless and horseless. I can't do a thing.

items.speaker: Will
items.text: What in the bloody hell is that? Some kind of mechanical freak?

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Not to worry, Brimley. Now, folks, take a look at this. Thanks to your generous donations, my experiments on smog removal have finally come to fruition.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Introducing the London Air Pollution Auto-Detecting Purifier MK. II! A high-power, multifunctional, air-cleaning machine!

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: The current model can only operate for three hours at a time, but I'll continue to improve its performance before the qualifiers begin. It's estimated to last a whole day by then.

items.speaker: Neighbor I
items.text: Wonderful! Simply wonderful!
A cheer erupts from the crowd.

items.speaker: Will
items.text: No more smog standin' in our way!

items.speaker: Neighbor I
items.text: Goodness, I can't remember the last time I saw the sun and breathed fresh air. I feel as though I've been rotting!
Amidst the raucous celebration, Brimley takes a moment to glance at Tooth Fairy, who is standing silently off to one side.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: It's an honor to see that sweet smile of yours, darl.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: I think I'm inspired somehow. I've always felt like a bit of an outsider in London, but this festive atmosphere makes me feel a sense of belonging.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: I totally understand.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Though I Awakened in London, my true home is the land down under, thousands of miles from here. In some ways, I'm an immigrant. This sense of belonging is a treasure.
Inside the sleepy car, the radio broadcasts a variety of live updates.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcast
items.text: Yes, as an East London resident, my chest swelled with pride when I learned that the Uluru Qualifiers would be held here. I couldn't wait to see what would happen.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member I
items.text: A-Achoo!

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member II
items.text: That's your ninth sneeze since we got here.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member I
items.text: Don't blame me! I didn't even wanna come! The Uluru Committee ignored my application to stay at the Australian headquarters. They couldn't find anyone willing to come to London with all this smog in the air.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member II
items.text: They didn't have much choice, either, mate. The Foundation's been preparing for the qualifiers in London for ages. We'll suffer huge financial losses if it's canceled.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member II
items.text: Someone has to make the trip to decide whether we should cut our losses or continue to throw money at it. You must've done something to be the lucky one who has to do the job.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member II
items.text: Holy ...!
The car screeches to a halt as a group of sooty critters scurry by the front bumper. As the shuffling subsides, the engine revs up again.

items.speaker: Driver
items.text: I do apologize. These little monsters are all over the streets these days.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member I
items.text: Haha, he sounds so calm. You'd think he was just talking about stray cats.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member I
items.text: You have to admire the stoicism of the Brits, especially in the face of all this. Honestly, this environment is totally unsuitable for any kind of outdoor activity.
The Foundation member says nothing, quietly jotting something down in a notebook.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member I
items.text: Hey, what are you doing?

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member II
items.text: Making note of the crash that almost happened. *sigh* These records will be used to decide if the qualifiers should be canceled. Someone has to be the doer since we already have a whiner on the team, eh?
With a sidelong glance at the scenery beyond the window, the man under the mask exhales softly.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member I
items.text: Look at all the decorations and posters. So much preparation for an event that won't even be held.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member II
items.text: I'm surprised they even wanna hold the qualifiers given the situation.
A gentle silence fills the car, its clarity as soft and blurred as the yellowish smog outside.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member I
items.text: Anyway, let's make it quick and get this job over with.

items.speaker: Foundation Branch Member I
items.text: Let me see. We need two things: evidence that proves the environment isn't suitable for holding the qualifiers, and the profiles of all the participating athletes. Then we can go home.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcast
items.text: Next, the changes made to Cross Street. Let's see what the local community has done to prepare for the upcoming event.
The driver reaches a trembling hand to the radio and quietly turns the volume knob to its minimum.
On the busy street, a crowd gathers around Mr. Fog and his purification machine. After some further iteration, its performance has greatly improved.
Beside the device, the sign originally reading "London Air Pollution Auto-Detecting Purifier MK. II" now reads "MK. III" thanks to a single additional brushstroke.

items.speaker: Crowd
items.text: Three!

items.speaker: Crowd
items.text: Two!

items.speaker: Crowd
items.text: One!

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Start!
He pushes the red button on the machine.
The contraption, pieced together from household goods, has a glass container housing a solid metal mechanical lung purifier. It comes to life with a deep rumble.
Bit by bit, the yellow smog hanging in the air is inhaled by its gaping vent.

items.speaker: Crowd
items.text: Wow!
Eyes wide with wonder, the people watch as the world around them gradually turns clearer.

items.speaker: Freddy the Rascal
items.text: Wow! Look, Dad! Are those clouds in the sky? They're so white and fluffy!

items.speaker: Will
items.text: The air's so fresh. I've never felt anythin' like it!

items.speaker: Neighbor I
items.text: Hey! I can even see Keaton's store fifty yards from here! Hellooo! See, Keaton's waving back!
A wave of joy ripples through the crowd as they erupt into excited conversation.
Tooth Fairy watches Mr. Fog. He's staring upward. There is no celebration from him, only a quiet contemplation.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: The first week is for planning, the second for execution, and the last for delivery and paperwork.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Looks like you've completed the tasks as scheduled.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Are you relieved?
Mr. Fog stands there, still staring at the blue sky above.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Ms. Tooth Fairy, the sun is so golden and warm.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Don't mind him. He's all over the place after working non-stop for the last few weeks. He's just trying to say he's happy, that's all.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: What about you? How do you feel?

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Me? The ranger's soul inside me has always wanted to gallop beneath the blazing sun!

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Yahooo!
Brimley charges forward, gliding merrily above the heads of those around him.
Tooth Fairy watches with a gentle smile. Then, something catches the corner of her eye.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Huh?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: A critter?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: No. Is that ... the black fog?

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: What's it doing here?
Guided by the traces of arcane energy, she takes a few steps over to the corner.
A faint, shadowy haze momentarily clouds her vision, vanishing just as suddenly as it came.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: I thought the black fog was a result of the increased density of regular smog in the air, but it seems I was wrong.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Mr. Fog's machine has cleaned up the smog around us, but the black fog's still here, and it's getting thicker. How curious.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: At least now, without the smog covering its trail, I can sense its movements more clearly.
Following her keen senses, Tooth Fairy silently slips into a narrow alleyway.
Her nostrils sting as she enters the trail of the black fog.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: *cough*
Doing her best to wave it off with her hand, she continues to follow the trail of the enigmatic presence.
Something tiny and black seems to shudder in a corner deep within the alley.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: What? What's that?
The black creature springs into motion, vanishing from her sight in the blink of an eye.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Hmm?
Now doesn't feel like the time to focus on that little dark lump.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: The smog's back.
The smog rolls back in, but this time it has taken on a thick, blackened quality, and it's accompanied by a handful of unexpected intruders.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: I did hear that these little things tend to gather in the quiet alleys of Cross Street. Perhaps they'd like a visit from the toothfairies.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: Slipped away at the first opportunity.
She can't make out where they went through the thickness of the smog.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: I knew it.
Slightly fatigued, she pauses to tidy up her hair.

items.speaker: Tooth Fairy
items.text: But what exactly was it?
